Mutating the Batting table to add in calculated statistics that are not inherent to the original table. 
```{r}
season <- Batting |>
  filter(yearID == 2025) |>
  group_by(playerID, yearID) |>
  summarise(across(c(AB, H, X2B, X3B, HR, BB, HBP, SF, SH, SO), sum),.groups = "drop")

season <- season |>
  mutate(
    PA = AB + BB + HBP + SF + SH,
    X1B = H - X2B - X3B - HR,
    AVG = H / AB,
    OBP = (H + BB + HBP) / (AB + BB + HBP + SF),
    SLG = (X1B + 2 * X2B + 3 * X3B + 4 * HR) / AB,
    OPS = OBP + SLG
  ) |> 
  filter(PA >= 300)
```

Aaron Judge leads both the OPS and OBP leaderboard for the 2025 season. Ohtani was second in OPS but dropped to 8th in OBP. Statistics were rounded to 3 dec and arranged in decending order by OPS/OBP.
```{r}
ops_leaderboard <- 
  season |>
  left_join(People |> select(playerID, nameFirst, nameLast), by = "playerID") |>
  select(nameFirst, nameLast, PA, AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS) |>
  mutate(across(AVG:OPS, \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  arrange(desc(OPS))

obp_leaderboard <- 
  season |>
  left_join(People |> select(playerID, nameFirst, nameLast), by = "playerID") |>
  select(nameFirst, nameLast, PA, AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS) |>
  mutate(across(AVG:OPS, \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  arrange(desc(OBP))
```

Batting_rates function was used to store the mutation of the Batting table with the additional statistics. Barry bonds has the top 4 spots in the top 10 OPS from the 2000 season onward. Aaron judge is the only player in the statcast era to crack the top 10 from 2000-present. He also holds the top 3 spots in the 2015-present top 10 OPS listing.
```{r}
batting_rates <- function(df) {
  df |>
    group_by(playerID, yearID) |>
    summarise(across(c(AB, H, X2B, X3B, HR, BB, HBP, SF, SH, SO), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
      PA  = AB + BB + HBP + SF + SH,
      X1B = H - X2B - X3B - HR,
      AVG = H / AB,
      OBP = (H + BB + HBP) / (AB + BB + HBP + SF),
      SLG = (X1B + 2 * X2B + 3 * X3B + 4 * HR) / AB,
      OPS = OBP + SLG
    )
}
source(here::here("R", "batting_rates.R"))

Batting |> 
  filter(yearID >= 2000) |>
  batting_rates() |>
  filter(PA >= 502) |>
  slice_max(OPS, n = 10) |>
  left_join(People |> select(playerID, nameFirst, nameLast), by = "playerID") |>
  select(nameFirst, nameLast, yearID, OBP, SLG, OPS)

#Top during Statcast era
Batting |>
  filter(yearID >= 2015) |>
  batting_rates() |>
  filter(PA >= 502) |>
  slice_max(OPS, n = 10) |>
  left_join(People |> select(playerID, nameFirst, nameLast), by = "playerID") |>
  select(nameFirst, nameLast, yearID, OPS, SLG, OBP, PA)
```
